daily_health.title: Daily Health Check Tools
daily_health.description: Job log and system value tools for daily IBM i health monitoring. Use with 'performance' toolset for complete coverage.

joblog_info.description:
Troubleshoot job errors by retrieving job log messages. Returns
message ID, type, severity, text, second-level text, and the
originating program/module/procedure. Use job_name '*' for the
current job; otherwise pass a qualified name (number/user/name).
Filter by message_type_filter: 'ESCAPE' for errors, 'DIAGNOSTIC'
for warnings, 'COMPLETION' for success confirmations. Use after
job_info to investigate why a specific job failed or is stuck.

parameters.name: job_name
parameters.description: Qualified job name (e.g., '123456/MYUSER/MYJOB') or '*' for the current job

parameters.name: row_limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of messages to return (1-200)

system_value_lookup.description:
Find system configuration values by name pattern using LIKE
syntax (use % as wildcard). Returns both numeric and character
values — unlike system_values in the performance toolset which
returns only numeric values for all settings, this tool searches
by pattern for targeted lookup. Useful patterns: '%SEC%' for
security, '%LOG%' for logging, '%LMT%' for limits, '%AUD%'
for auditing. Use when investigating a specific config area
rather than reviewing all settings.

parameters.name: name_pattern
parameters.description: Pattern to match system value names (e.g., '%LMT%', '%SEC%', 'QCCSID', '%AUD%')

system_status.description:
First-call system health check. Returns CPU utilization (total,
interactive, batch, database), main storage size and usage, system
ASP capacity, active job counts, and temporary storage consumption.
Use as the starting point before drilling into memory_pools or
active_job_info for specifics. See also: system_activity for
real-time per-pool breakdowns.

system_activity.description:
Real-time per-pool CPU utilization, database faulting, and active
thread counts. Unlike system_status (which gives overall
system-level metrics), this shows activity broken down by memory
pool for identifying which pool is under pressure right now.
See also: memory_pools for pool sizing and configuration.

remote_connections.description:
Count of established TCP connections from remote clients, excluding
loopback (127.0.0.1 and ::1). Use to gauge how many external
sessions (ODBC, SSH, FTP, HTTP) are active on the system. A sudden
spike can indicate runaway connection pooling or unauthorized
access.

memory_pools.description:
Memory pool sizing, thread utilization, and faulting rates for
each pool (*MACHINE, *BASE, *INTERACT, *SPOOL, and user-defined
pools). Returns current/defined/reserved size, max active threads,
and current thread count. Use after system_status to drill into
pool-level memory pressure. See also: system_activity for
real-time per-pool CPU and faulting.

temp_storage_buckets.description:
Named temporary storage bucket usage (current and peak sizes).
Temporary storage on IBM i is auxiliary storage used by jobs for
internal objects like open data paths and SQL cursors. High temp
storage often indicates runaway queries or jobs that are not
releasing resources. See also: unnamed_temp_storage for the
aggregate of unnamed buckets.

unnamed_temp_storage.description:
Aggregate current and peak size of unnamed temporary storage
buckets. Unnamed buckets are internal system allocations not tied
to a named category. Large unnamed temp storage usage can signal
system-level issues that are harder to trace to individual jobs.
See also: temp_storage_buckets for a breakdown by named category.

http_server.description:
Performance metrics for all HTTP server instances running on IBM i
(Apache, IWS, etc.). Returns connections (normal and SSL),
active/idle threads, total requests, rejected requests, bytes
sent/received, and cache vs non-cache processing times. IBM i HTTP
servers power web services, REST APIs, and admin consoles.

system_values.description:
All system values (QSYS2.SYSTEM_VALUE_INFO) that have a numeric
value, including performance-relevant settings like QMAXACTLVL
(max active jobs), QBASACTLVL (base pool activity level), QMCHPOOL
(machine pool size), and QTOTJOB (total jobs). Use to verify
performance-related system configuration. Returns name/value pairs
only for values with non-null numeric data.

collection_services.description:
Current configuration of IBM i Collection Services, the built-in
performance data collection framework. Returns collection status,
interval, retention period, library, and active categories. Use to
verify that performance data collection is enabled and properly
configured before analyzing historical trends. See also:
collection_categories for per-category interval detail.

collection_categories.description:
Per-category collection intervals for Collection Services. Shows
which data categories (e.g., *SYSLVL, *JOBMI, *POOL, *DISK, *IOP)
are being collected and at what interval. Use to verify granularity
of performance data collection or to check if a specific category
is active. See also: collection_services for overall Collection
Services status.

active_job_info.description:
Rank active jobs by CPU consumption to find the heaviest consumers.
Defaults to QUSRWRK and QSYSWRK subsystems (where most user work
and system server jobs run). Returns CPU time, job name, user,
function, type, status, and more. Use after system_status shows
high CPU to identify which specific jobs are responsible.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of top CPU consumers to return

sysadmin_discovery.title: Sys Admin Discovery
sysadmin_discovery.description: High-level summaries and counts for services.

list_service_categories.description:
Summarize all SQL Service categories with service counts.
Starting point for exploring available IBM i services. Returns
category name and count, sorted by highest count. Use before
list_services_by_category to pick a category to drill into.

count_services_by_schema.description:
Count SQL Services by schema (library) to see which system
libraries provide services. QSYS2 and SYSTOOLS are the primary
providers. Use to discover which schema to explore further
with list_services_by_schema.

count_services_by_sql_object_type.description:
Categorize services by SQL object type (VIEW, PROCEDURE,
TABLE FUNCTION, SCALAR FUNCTION, TABLE). TABLE FUNCTIONs
are the most common high-value services (ACTIVE_JOB_INFO,
OBJECT_STATISTICS, etc.). VIEWs are simpler read-only queries.
Use to understand the implementation landscape of available
services.

list_categories_for_schema.description:
Show which service categories exist within a specific schema.
Use to explore a single schema's capabilities (e.g., 'What
troubleshooting services does QSYS2 provide?'). Complement to
list_service_categories which shows categories across all
schemas.

sysadmin_browse.title: Sys Admin Browse
sysadmin_browse.description: Explore services by category, schema, and SQL object type; validate metadata.

list_services_by_category.description:
Browse all services within a specific category (e.g., Work
Management, Security, Performance). Returns schema, name,
SQL object type, and release info. Unlike search_services_by_name
(keyword search), this is category-based exploration. Category
must be an exact match from list_service_categories — use that
tool first to get valid category names.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Exact value of SERVICE_CATEGORY to filter by.

list_services_by_schema.description:
Explore all services provided by a specific schema (library).
Returns category, name, SQL object type, and release info.
Unlike list_services_by_category (category-based), this groups
by schema — useful for answering "What can I do with QSYS2?"
Most services live in QSYS2; SYSTOOLS has utility functions.

parameters.name: schema_name
parameters.description: Schema name (library), e.g., QSYS2 or SYSTOOLS.

list_services_by_sql_object_type.description:
Find services by SQL implementation type (VIEW, PROCEDURE,
TABLE FUNCTION, SCALAR FUNCTION, TABLE). TABLE FUNCTIONs are
the most useful for querying (parameterized, tabular output).
SCALAR FUNCTIONs are typically helpers used inside other
queries. Use to find all services of a specific type.

parameters.name: sql_object_type
parameters.description: SQL object type to filter by.

sysadmin_search.title: Sys Admin Search
sysadmin_search.description: Search capabilities for service names and example usage.

search_services_by_name.description:
Find SQL Services by keyword in the service name. Uses
case-insensitive LIKE '%keyword%' matching — partial names
work (e.g., 'JOB' finds ACTIVE_JOB_INFO, JOB_INFO, etc.).
Unlike where_is_service (exact name lookup), this is for
discovery when you don't know the full name. Use first to
find candidates, then get_service_example for usage details.

parameters.name: name_contains
parameters.description: Substring to search for in SERVICE_NAME.

where_is_service.description:
Locate a specific SQL Service by exact name and return its
schema, category, SQL object type, and release info. Unlike
search_services_by_name (partial keyword match), this requires
the exact service name but is case-insensitive. Use when you
know the service name and need to find which schema provides
it and its object type.

search_examples_for_keyword.description:
Find services whose example SQL contains a keyword or phrase.
Case-insensitive search across all service examples. Returns
only the first 300 characters of each example — use
get_service_example for the full text. Useful for finding
learning examples (e.g., search 'AUTHORITY' to find services
with security-related example SQL).

parameters.name: keyword
parameters.description: Keyword or phrase to search for within EXAMPLE text.

get_service_example.description:
Get the complete example SQL for a specific service. Unlike
search_examples_for_keyword (which returns 300-char snippets),
this returns the full example text. Some services have no
example — result will be NULL. Requires exact schema and
service name; use search_services_by_name first if unsure of
the exact name.

parameters.name: schema_name
parameters.description: Schema name containing the service (e.g., QSYS2).
